claims.paper_reference: Method: fixed Module-LWE parameters and concrete attack-cost estimation
claims.statement: The implementation uses k=6, d=256, n=m=1536, q=2^32, p=65537 and sigma_key=3.2. The complete recorded seven-attack estimate has minimum 136.475 bits against a required estimator threshold of 128.1 bits.
claims.scope: Generic flattened-LWE analysis under the pinned estimator distributions and cost models. Reduction attacks use the recorded ADPS16 quantum model and GSA; coded-BKW retains its native operation-count convention. This is not an actual-finite-CDT, module-specific, side-channel, implementation, all-attack or worst-case security proof.
required_for_original_claim: Security claims require an explicit instantiated encryption distribution, attack applicability and threat model in addition to estimator arithmetic.
Every reported attack cost is tied to its recorded inputs, source, environment and native cost convention.

claims.paper_reference: Method: profile-bound packing and canonical ciphertext serialization
claims.statement: At k=6, up to 240 retained data coefficients and 16 tags fit into one degree-256 polynomial and a 7,168-byte ciphertext; the 480-coefficient raw representation uses two ciphertexts totaling 14,336 bytes.
claims.scope: Encoded-payload arithmetic only. At 250 kbit/s the ideal single-hop payload serialization times are 229.376 ms and 458.752 ms. Tickets, authentication, headers, fragmentation, contention, retries and computation are additional. Changing retained support within one polynomial does not shorten its ciphertext.
required_for_original_claim: Complete communication and latency claims require the full protocol accounting boundary and matching measured service costs.
Signal utility requires aggregate-domain error evaluation on the stated input distribution.

claims.paper_reference: Method: additive encryption, centered data decoding and aggregate reconstruction
claims.statement: Ciphertext addition and decryption recover sums of encoded quantized data and tag coefficients modulo p; the data no-wrap bound permits interpreting admitted data coordinates as signed integer sums.
claims.scope: Host functional encryption/aggregation tests support encoded-domain correctness under the stated no-wrap and decoding assumptions. Rounded integer lifting, coefficient selection and quantization make physical-signal reconstruction a separate approximation. Functional trials do not establish a 2^-128 tail probability.
required_for_original_claim: Aggregate-signal accuracy is characterized against the true sum, with profile, batch size, input scaling and rounding conventions identified.
Execution records identify the exact source, encryption parameters, provider and input traces.

claims.paper_reference: Method: signed roster authorization and sink aggregate verification
claims.statement: Signed tickets bind the operating profile, context, nonces, encryption parameters and exact participant roster. Real-provider host trials exercise legal acceptance, gateway-tampering rejection and persistent replay rejection.
claims.scope: Functional protocol evidence under trusted source/sink and secret-derivation assumptions. Gateway-held HMACs filter external pollution but do not secure a compromised gateway. The authenticated plaintext path is not confidential. Q_v/p^16 is one conditional tag-guessing contribution, not a complete-system security level or measured attack-detection probability.
required_for_original_claim: The integrity model requires one distinct report per authorized ticket/source offset, protected derivation secrets, valid primitive assumptions and correctly scoped decoding bounds.
A security reduction requires its uniform-rejection, hash-binding and persistent-state assumptions.
Deployment documentation identifies the ML-DSA provider, context/key binding, nonce handling and supported adversary capabilities.

claims.paper_reference: Method: durable source-emission cache and at-most-once sink acceptance
claims.statement: SourceEmissionStore transactionally binds a raw-payload digest and retains the first committed envelope for each ticket/source/nonce. Retries return the cached signed ticket and blocks. ReplayStore reserves the ticket digest only after validation and before result release.
claims.scope: SQLite host persistence and targeted regression tests. Concurrent same-payload callers receive the committed envelope; different payloads are rejected. Storage rollback/deletion invalidates the emission/replay assumptions. The implementation is not an embedded anti-rollback driver; at-most-once acceptance does not itself supply durable exactly-once application delivery.
required_for_original_claim: Embedded deployment requires protected nonvolatile storage, anti-rollback and crash-recovery evidence.
Application delivery requires a transactional result/outbox and an idempotent trusted consumer where loss after acceptance is unacceptable.

claims.paper_reference: Correctness: exact finite-CDT single-batch decoding bound
claims.statement: The executed k=6 finite-CDT calculation covers (sigma_enc,Nmax)=(3.2,16),(3.4,14),(3.6,12), shared-key noise products and scaling carry. The 42-choice single-batch union log2 upper endpoint is approximately -130.5101732.
claims.scope: Outward-interval calculation for the implemented finite sampler, jointly over random key generation and fresh honest batch noises. Configuration and roster selection precede fresh batch noise. It does not establish every-fixed-key, arbitrary observed-history conditional, malicious-ciphertext, lifetime, memory or controller guarantees. Fresh calculations require Sage-enabled Python.
required_for_original_claim: The probability statement identifies the exact CDT masses, independence assumptions, decoder/carry margin and interval endpoints.
Task-level claims use an explicit horizon and attempt count; confidentiality, forgery and network-loss claims remain separate.

claims.paper_reference: Correctness: exact-rational finite-task decoding risk budget
claims.statement: For a predeclared cap B on covered fresh-noise batch attempts, the checker computes min(1,B*U) from the pinned single-batch upper bound U and compares it exactly with the selected task risk.
verification_commands: python tools/check_decoding_horizon.py --batches 6 --target-bits 128 # expected exit 2: risk budget exceeded
claims.scope: Executed budgets permit at most 5 attempts at target 2^-128 (6 is not certified) and at most 1458 at 2^-120 (300 passes). Independence between batch failures is not assumed. Fresh-noise and preselection conditions apply to every counted attempt. A failed budget comparison is not an observed decoding failure, a uniform fixed-key/history result or a lifetime guarantee.
required_for_original_claim: A deployment states its task duration, attempt cap, profile/roster selection and key lifecycle.
Fresh-noise retries and reencryptions count as attempts.
Uniform fixed-key/history claims require a certificate valid for that conditioning.

claims.statement: The executed fidelity study evaluates 72 declared synthetic cases against the true integer-count source sum: 54 capacity-admissible cases and 18 explicitly inadmissible diagnostics.
claims.scope: Exact integer arrays and recomputed metrics separate rounded-lifting aggregation, selection and quantization effects in a declared order. Zero-reference PRD is explicitly undefined. Frozen source and raw inputs are available. The study does not establish calibrated physical units, a real sensor population, a universal distortion threshold, encryption/decryption performance or a full-system certificate.
required_for_original_claim: Physical-signal claims require an identified sensor corpus, units/scaling, normalization, transform/rounding, support and boundary conventions.
Utility-constrained control claims require actual signal values and distortion feedback in the closed-loop evaluation.

claims.paper_reference: Method: controlled HMM, robust drift admission and conditional stability
claims.statement: ControlledHMM, robust action scoring, DPP/HYS and evidence gates are implemented. The network campaign uses an explicitly uncalibrated synthetic fixture and records uncertified decisions.
verification_commands: python -m daahe replay-control --config configs/control_synthetic.json --telemetry examples/telemetry_synthetic.csv --method da-ahe --allow-synthetic --output runs/reviewer-synthetic-control.json
claims.scope: Functional and analytic implementation evidence. Artifact identity checks do not establish proof validity. Conditional mean-square ultimate boundedness does not imply forward invariance, zero QoS violations or safety under arbitrary denial of service. Online floating-point drift comparisons need conservative numerical-error treatment for deployment certification.
required_for_original_claim: A deployment certificate identifies separate training, heldout calibration and evaluation traces and the complete observation model.
Uniform state-error/transition bounds, the exact action library, P_V, Z_cert, gamma/beta, fallback nonemptiness and invariance or exit handling require reviewed evidence.
Online adaptation and bounded adversarial observations must be included in the validity scope.
Attribution to belief and robustness requires matched same-envelope controls including DPP with the same filter, a no-belief robust filter and nominal belief control.

claims.paper_reference: Implementation: compiled core harness and deployment memory requirements
claims.statement: The selected rank-6 core build reports 5,624-byte load sections and 20,608-byte static RAM with benchmark stack reservations. Physical-board samples remain zero.
claims.scope: Core compilation and host known-answer evidence only. They do not establish complete-protocol stack high-water, per-role peak SRAM, network/OS memory lifetimes or a full-role workspace certificate.
required_for_original_claim: Complete embedded resource claims require linked per-role firmware, ELF/map and compiler/OS identities.
Stack, buffers, cryptographic/transform/authentication workspaces and network/interrupt paths require physical stress capture and lifetime accounting.
Action workspace, static SRAM, reserved stack and measured runtime peak must have distinct accounting boundaries.

claims.paper_reference: Evaluation: modeled service costs and physical measurement requirements
claims.statement: The network study reports declared modeled CPU and radio-transmit energy and exact ciphertext-payload serialization arithmetic. It contains no physical-board timing or power samples.
claims.scope: Cross-compilation and host known answers are distinct from physical timing/power. Simulation service times are explicit assumptions. CPU/TX accounting omits receive/listen, operating-system and other stated costs. Payload serialization is not complete operational latency or complete-protocol energy.
required_for_original_claim: Physical cost claims require complete rank-6 source/gateway/sink measurements with firmware identity, raw cycles and calibrated power traces.
The accounting boundary identifies ticket/signature/KDF/HMAC, source ledger, framing, relaying, receive/listen and OS/interrupt work.
Workload-weighted totals use costs measured or modeled under the same stated parameters and boundary.

claims.statement: The executed synthetic Python campaign compares all seven methods across 20 paired seeds at 3,000 sensors and 60 gateways, with 90 s of generation and 35 s of draining.
claims.scope: All 140 records, including failed deliveries, are retained. DA-AHE, HYS and the fixed nominal action have different admission/delivery/delay/cost tradeoffs; no overall dominance is established. Recovery is right-censored in every run and route repair was not triggered. Modeled invalid acceptance without HVE is not reliable delivery or an empirical forgery bound. The model is not an OMNeT++/INET, full radio, RPL or physical-board execution.
required_for_original_claim: Physical-network generalization requires measured service/channel calibration and an identified deployment workload.
Mechanism attribution requires matched offered opportunities, fidelity constraints and controls; repair efficacy requires an experiment that activates repair.
Reported delivery/loss/invalidity denominators, conditional delay, censoring and full cost boundaries remain explicit.
Inference beyond descriptive seed statistics requires a separately specified and executed statistical analysis.

claims.paper_reference: Reproducibility: public raw records, derived results and frozen-source checks
claims.statement: The public archive indexes 20 paired seeds, seven methods and 140 runs. The current result export is recomputed from all per-seed rows and binds security, fidelity, horizon and execution records by hash.
claims.scope: Archive checks establish byte integrity and raw-to-summary consistency; rebuilding the export does not rerun the network. Frozen-source byte replay has a documented environment boundary, with macOS ARM64/Python3.12.10 replay and separate Linux raw recomputation. Hashes do not authenticate physical measurements or establish mathematical certification.
required_for_original_claim: Each independent execution retains its exact source/config/input/provider/environment identity and receipt.
All methods, failed deliveries, censored outcomes and replay-environment differences remain available.
Generated records are hash-bound only after actual execution; configuration and workflow presence are not execution evidence.
